chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Al-Qasim ibn Urwah, from Zurarah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The woman whose husband has died, it is not for her to perfume herself nor to adorn herself until her waiting period (iddah) of four months and ten days is completed.

key_terms.الْمُتَوَفَّى عَنْهَا: The woman whose husband has died (widow)

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period (iddah) for a widow in Shia Islam and what are the restrictions?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi, narrated through the chain of Zurarah to Imam al-Sadiq, clarifies the behavioral restrictions during the four-month-and-ten-day iddah of a widow who has been consummated with. It emphasizes modesty and mourning by prohibiting the use of perfume and adornment, reflecting the Shia scholarly view that these acts signify joy or readiness for remarriage, which is subdued during the waiting period. This ruling is derived directly from the Quranic verse in Surah Al-Baqarah, reinforcing the spiritual and social dimensions of grief and transition in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Al Qasim Bin Urwat, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The woman widowed from her husband, it is not for her that she perfumes, nor adorns until she fulfils her waiting period of four months and ten days’.
en.sarwar: 10. Humayd has narrated from ibn Sama‘ah from Muhammad ibn abu Hamzah from abu Ayyub from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “A woman came to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, to ask for a fatwa about spending the night in another house; her husband had died.

He (the Imam) said, ‘In the time of ignorance widows had to sit in mourning for twelve months. When Muhammad, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, was sent he felt sympathy for their weakness and reduced it (mourning) to four months and ten days but you do not bear it patiently.’”
